- When sentiment is consistently negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–7 day horizons.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 5–10 day horizons.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model often holds too high; adjust downward by 1–4% for 10+ day forecasts.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often lags; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–7 day horizons to align with sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates by 3–8% when sentiment is neutral or bearish; apply 3–6% downward correction.
